title: Area of Parallelograms and Triangles
prerequisites: Formula for the area of a rectangle.
Idea of the height or altitude of a figure.

topics.title: Figures on the Same Base and Between the Same Parallels
topics.quick_summary: Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area, and a triangle in that position has half the area of the parallelogram.
topics.real_life: Sliding the top of a stack of paper sideways changes the shape from a rectangle to a slanted parallelogram, but not the amount of paper — area unchanged.

detailed.definition: Two figures are said to be on the same base and between the same parallels if they share a base and their opposite sides or vertices lie on a line parallel to that base.
detailed.key_idea: Area depends only on base and perpendicular height, never on how slanted the figure is. Every result in this chapter is a restatement of that single fact.
detailed.working_principle: Since the parallels are a fixed distance apart, all such figures have the same height. With base and height both equal, their areas must be equal.
applications: A median of a triangle divides it into two triangles of equal area.
A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two congruent triangles of equal area.
The diagonals of a parallelogram divide it into four triangles of equal area.

points: Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area.
A triangle and a parallelogram on the same base and between the same parallels: triangle = ½ parallelogram.
Triangles on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area.
A median divides a triangle into two triangles of equal area.
Equal areas do not imply congruence.
mistakes: Confusing equal area with congruence; equal-area figures may have very different shapes.
Using a slant side as the height instead of the perpendicular distance.
Forgetting the factor of ½ when comparing a triangle with a parallelogram.
topics.memory_hook: 'Same base, same parallels, same area' — slant does not change the size.
topics.advanced: This is the geometric ancestor of Cavalieri's principle: two solids with equal cross-sectional areas at every height have equal volume. It is what makes the volume of an oblique cylinder equal to that of a right one.

formulas.name: Area of a Parallelogram and a Triangle
formulas.formula: Area of parallelogram = base × height;  Area of triangle = ½ × base × height
formulas.variables: base = any chosen side, height = perpendicular distance from that side to the opposite side or vertex.
formulas.when_to_use: For any parallelogram or triangle where a base and its corresponding height are known.
formulas.common_mistakes: Using a slant side as the height instead of the perpendicular distance.
formulas.shortcut: Any side may be taken as the base, provided the height is measured perpendicular to it.
